headings.title: Introduction and Legal Foundations of Patient Assessment Documentation
headings.content: Patient assessment documentation forms the permanent legal and clinical record of a client's health journey. Beyond charting daily observations, it serves as the primary communication bridge between multidisciplinary healthcare team members. In Nigerian clinical settings, as regulated by the Nursing and Midwifery Council of Nigeria (NMCN), accurate records protect both the practitioner and the patient. Courts view written notes as the definitive account of care given; if an intervention is not documented, legally, it was never performed.

headings.title: Core Components of a Comprehensive Patient Assessment Record
headings.content:
A thorough assessment record integrates both subjective data gathered from the patient and objective data discovered through physical examination and diagnostics. 

- **Biographical Data**: Age, gender, occupation, and basic identifiers.
- **Chief Complaint**: The primary reason for seeking care, stated in the patient's own words.
- **History of Present Illness**: A chronological timeline of symptom progression.
- **Review of Systems**: Systematic inquiry into each body system to uncover unmentioned symptoms.
- **Physical Examination Findings**: Measurable data including vital signs, inspection, palpation, percussion, and auscultation results.

headings.title: Formats and Systems of Nursing Documentation
headings.content:
Different clinical environments utilize distinct structural frameworks to organize client data. Narrative charting tells a sequential story of care but can become lengthy and disorganized. Problem-Oriented Medical Records (POMR) group data around specific client issues using the SOAP format.

| Format | Primary Structure | Common Use Case |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Narrative** | Chronological paragraph style | General wards, emergency updates |
| **SOAP** | Subjective, Objective, Assessment, Plan | Medical-surgical nursing notes |
| **PIE** | Problem, Intervention, Evaluation | Long-term care and focused tracking |
| **DAR** | Data, Action, Response | Focus charting formats |

headings.title: Principles of Accurate, Objective, and Timely Recording
headings.content:
Clear communication requires adherence to strict documentation principles. Notes must be factual and free from personal bias or judgmental labels. For instance, writing "patient is uncooperative" is subjective and vague; instead, record specific behaviors such as "patient refused morning medication and stated 'I do not want to take these pills today.'"

Timeliness is equally critical. Documenting care immediately after completion prevents memory lapses and reduces the risk of omissions. If an error occurs on paper records, draw a single line through the mistake, write "mistaken entry" above it, and sign it—never use correction fluid or erase text.

headings.title: Common Documentation Errors and How to Avoid Them
headings.content: Failure to document adequately compromises patient safety and exposes clinicians to liability. Common pitfalls include charting ahead of time, omitting critical assessment findings, and using unauthorized abbreviations. Pre-charting—documenting an intervention before it is actually performed—falsifies the medical record and is considered professional misconduct. Furthermore, nurses must rely on approved institutional abbreviation lists to prevent medication and treatment misinterpretations.

headings.title: Confidentiality, Privacy, and Data Protection Regulations
headings.content: Patient health information is legally protected and must remain strictly confidential. In Nigeria, the Nigeria Data Protection Regulation (NDPR) governs how digital and physical health records are collected, stored, and processed. Nurses have an ethical duty to safeguard passwords, log out of Electronic Health Records (EHR) terminals when leaving workstations, and avoid discussing client conditions in public areas. Breaching confidentiality erodes patient trust and carries severe disciplinary consequences.
